shell.source: CAD plate: outer architectural lines (walls, windows, sills, columns) of this drawing. For a floor above the twin's annex the CAD outline wins over the photo twin's massing; it is exported as drawn, not fitted into the twin body.
shell.window_note: Facade openings from AR-WINDOW / STR. GLAZING lines within 1.2 m of the plate edge, parallel lines merged into one opening (position = centre, width along the facade). Sill and head heights are not in the CAD (plan only); see the assumptions file.

ceiling_plan.note: AC grilles / diffusers: nothing drawn (ARCIL has empty layers named AC Grill and AC-RA-GRILLE).

site_fit.about: CAD plan (x east, y north in the drawing, metres) to the map's local ENU metres round the atlas pin: ENU = R(rot) * (p - plate_centroid) + footprint_centroid + [dx, dy]. Twin GLB local (Blender x, y) to ENU: ENU = R(phi) * b + C.
site_fit.why: The footprint is close to a rectangle, so a 180 deg turn scores almost the same. The chosen one puts the CAD's lift core toward the street front (bearing 146), where the twin's entrance is. The drawing's own north arrow does not agree with the footprint by about 100 deg, so it is treated as project north.
site_fit.front_shift_why: Slid back along the long axis so Volt's front wall meets the twin's front (the annex face with the entrance porch). The real footprint and the CAD put the front about 1.6 m further out than the twin does.

via_volt_frame.how: tenant plan -> Volt plan frame from matched columns (cad/plate_fit.py), then Volt's own site_fit. Composed exactly; same formula as Volt's site_fit.

podium_about: Two-storey glass block (ground and first floor, 9.7 m like the annex) where the CAD floor runs beyond the twin. Plan coordinates.
